skills.name: correction-of-errors
skills.description: Run a blameless post-incident review (Correction of Errors / CoE) covering incident summary, customer impact, timeline, facts, Five Whys, root cause, detection and prevention gaps, action items, and follow-up. Refuses to stop at "human error" — asks why the system allowed the human action to create customer impact. Use after any production incident, customer-impacting outage, or process failure; or when the user mentions "CoE", "Correction of Errors", "postmortem", "post-incident review", "RCA", or "Five Whys".

skills.name: dissent-before-commit
skills.description: Gate one already-authorized action that is now scheduled to fire, by re-checking every objection raised at authoring time against what has changed since, then forcing the single strongest current case to be addressed by a change to the action or accepted with a named tradeoff a named person owns. For irreversible actions an accepted tradeoff is not sufficient and the recommendation becomes pause. Catches a team pointing at an old dissent discussion as proof concerns were heard when nobody has rechecked it against current state. Use when a migration cut-over, deprecation, launch, contract termination, staff release, or data deletion is queued and was approved weeks or months ago. Trigger phrases include before we cut over, one-way door, is this still the right call, any last objections, pre-commit review, point of no return, we already discussed the risks.

skills.name: initiative-thesis-review
skills.description: Decide whether one initiative is still worth pursuing by testing its tenets — the "if we are wrong about X, we should stop" statements — against external evidence consulted before the dashboard, and refusing to return continue while any tenet is invalid. Requires documented external context changes as an input, because without them a tenet check collapses into a metrics check. Exists to catch the case where output metrics sit inside target while the belief the initiative was funded on has quietly collapsed, because the team narrowed what it measures to the part still working. For one initiative, not allocation across several. Trigger phrases include should we still be doing this, is this still the right bet, thesis check, pivot or kill, tenets review, do we still believe this, the numbers look fine but.

skills.name: launch-readiness-review
skills.description: Gate the launch of a feature, product, or initiative by diffing the current build state against the original PRFAQ contract. Emits one of go / no_go / conditional_go / defer with a PRFAQ drift report, predicted failure modes (pre-mortem), risk register delta, and rollback testability check. The named failure mode is PRFAQ drift — the gap between authoring-time promise and ship-time reality, where the surface signal (features shipped match the PRFAQ scope) hides that the customer outcome the PRFAQ promised is not being delivered. Use when an artifact authorized by a PRFAQ or six-page narrative is approaching launch; or when the user mentions "launch readiness", "go/no-go", "ship review", "pre-launch review", or "launch gate".

skills.name: leadership-principles-reviewer
skills.description: Evaluate a proposal, project, PRFAQ, or six-page narrative against Amazon-style leadership principles. Surfaces strongest and weakest alignment, contradictions, missing evidence, and risks hidden by optimism. Use when reviewing a PRFAQ before submission, when stress-testing a strategy doc, when a proposal feels "too clean", or when the user mentions "LP review", "leadership principles", "stress test", "red team", or "pre-mortem".

skills.name: lifecycle-navigator
skills.description: Read governance.yaml, identify the next required Amazonian skill given the bet's current state, and route the operator either through superpowers:brainstorming (when present) or a minimal native questioning loop (when not). The named failure mode is phase laundering — recommending an advanced-phase interrogative skill against manifest fields that are themselves assumption-tagged from bootstrap, so the recommended stress test runs on laundered state. Refuses confirmatory invocation. Use at session start once governance.yaml exists, when the operator asks "what should I do next", or when they mention "lifecycle navigator", "next step", "what's next", "where am I in the chain", "PDLC flow", or "manage me through the suite".

skills.name: multi-persona-roundtable
skills.description: Stress-test one proposal from several fixed viewpoints that each own a kill criterion, run as separate isolated turns rather than one pass, so you get productive disagreement instead of an averaged opinion. Produces an append-only deliberation log and a verdict of ship, refine, or kill with the specific blocker named. Use when a proposal looks good and you suspect it will die on contact with ownership, funding, operations, or the people it claims to serve. Trigger phrases include roundtable, stress test this idea, red team, evaluate from multiple perspectives, poke holes in this, will this actually ship, pre-mortem, devil's advocate, panel review.

skills.name: portfolio-reallocation-review
skills.description: Review the allocation of capacity across every initiative a team runs at once by constructing the portfolio you would authorize from scratch today — same total capacity, same option set — before looking at the one you actually have, and treating the gap as the finding. Refuses to run if the hypothetical was built with the current allocation in view, if any initiative lacks a dated forward-looking case, or if a no-change outcome is not justified item by item. Exists to catch the portfolio that is the residue of accumulated past decisions rather than one anyone would choose today, which no per-initiative review can detect because each initiative returns a defensible answer. For three or more initiatives at once. Trigger phrases include portfolio review, bet allocation, what should we stop doing, are we spread too thin, nothing ever gets killed, planning cycle allocation.

skills.name: portfolio-review
skills.description: Stress-test a team's collective portfolio of bets across a period. Asks not "is each bet still right?" (that is `tenets-review`) but "given everything we know now, is the allocation across all of our current bets coherent?" Emits per-bet recommendations (continue / wind_down / amplify / hold / pivot), a zero-based reallocation comparison, and an explicit drift report. The named failure mode is portfolio drift — the portfolio that exists now is the residue of accumulated past decisions, not the portfolio anyone would intentionally author today; the surface signal (stable composition, defensible per-bet stories) hides incoherent marginal allocation. Use when a period closes and cross-bet allocation is up for review; or when the user mentions "portfolio review", "OKR cycle", "bet allocation", "investment review", or "kill list".

skills.name: principles-alignment-review
skills.description: Review a drafted proposal against a principle set the caller supplies — company values, engineering tenets, a funder's criteria, a team charter — and report where it aligns, where it is silent, and where it invokes one principle to excuse skipping another. The principle set is a required input with no default, and the review cannot come back with everything strong. Its distinctive output is the contradictions, found between principles and invisible to a principle-by-principle read. One reader applying one declared set, not several viewpoints arguing. Use when a proposal is about to be submitted, or when a document reads too clean. Trigger phrases include principles review, values review, review against our principles, stress test this proposal, red team this doc, adversarial review, does this hold up, pre-mortem this memo.

skills.name: repo-state-import
skills.description: Lift a brownfield repo's current governance state into a structured governance.yaml manifest. Conducts a guided interview over tenets, success metrics, live mechanisms, period goals, dissent history, and prior interviews; refuses to emit any field without an evidence tag from the set fact / assumption / inference / open_question; refuses to claim a field is a fact without a non-null source. The informal named risk is brownfield laundering — a populated manifest read by downstream skills as if it had passed governance gates when it never did. Use when first deploying the Amazonian suite onto an existing repo, or when re-importing after material changes; or when the user mentions "bootstrap", "onboard a repo", "lift state", "governance.yaml", "import existing state", or "brownfield deploy".

skills.name: risk_review
skills.description: Prevent common civic-tech mistakes and enforce guardrails.

skills.name: roundtable-facilitator
skills.description: Orchestrate a multi-turn, multi-persona evaluation of a civic innovation idea. Each persona takes a separate turn with real research, writes to a persistent conversation log, and the facilitator manages phase transitions, challenge routing, and consensus detection.

skills.name: roundtable-persona
skills.description: Template for individual persona turns in a roundtable evaluation. Each subagent loads this skill to understand its output format, research obligations, and behavioral constraints.

skills.name: tenets-review
skills.description: Stress-test whether a product or initiative is still worth pursuing by checking its tenets ("if we're wrong about X, stop") against current external context and metrics. Emits one of continue / kill / pivot / escalate. Refuses to let metrics speak for the thesis — the named failure mode is metric satisficing, where output metrics sit within target while the underlying bet has collapsed. Use when external context shifts, on annual review, or when the user mentions "tenets review", "kill criteria", "thesis check", "should we still be doing this", or "pivot or kill".

skills.name: working-backwards-prfaq
skills.description: Turn an idea into a PRFAQ (Amazon Working Backwards) packet — press release, customer FAQ, internal FAQ, MVP boundary, success metrics, risks, decision recommendation, and open questions. Use when defining a new product, feature, or internal initiative; when an idea needs sharpening before engineering or design starts; or when the user mentions PRFAQ, press release, working backwards, product definition, product brief, or product discovery.

skills.name: ambitious-goal-grading
skills.description: Grade whether a period's goal targets were set at an honest difficulty, not whether they were hit — reconcile every goal the period authorized against the ones submitted, recompute any target that moved mid-period against its original, require named surprise evidence for anything hit at or above 100%, and separate a target set too high from a plan that broke. Exists because a grading submission arrives pre-filtered — only the goals that were hit, with targets already revised, and the misses quietly dropped. Use at quarter or year end, when next period's targets are being set, or when a team keeps hitting everything. Trigger phrases include sandbagged, stretch goal, goal calibration, OKR scoring, grade the goals, were our targets right, did we set the bar too low, we hit 100% of our goals.

skills.name: anchored-rubric-design
skills.description: Design the scale for judging model output — fields that trade off against each other so one cheap trick can't max the score, numbered bands with worked anchors instead of an unanchored 1-10, each field typed rule-computed or LLM-judged, and the composite as deterministic arithmetic rather than an LLM's overall number. Produces a rubric spec; running one across candidates is `llm-behavior-benchmark`. Use before benchmarking, evaluating, or grading any model behavior — review-comment quality, empathy, concision, refusal quality, brand voice, teaching style. Trigger phrases include design a rubric, scoring criteria, LLM as judge, how should we grade this, evaluation dimensions, judge prompt, score the outputs, our scores are all the same.

skills.name: auditable-scoring-model
skills.description: Audit a statistical prediction — a price, rating, duration, or probability fitted from historical records — so target leakage is caught by a failing assertion rather than by an implausibly good validation score. Installs an allowlist assertion over feature names, structural separation between features and ground truth, a value scan over model outputs, and frozen calibration bounds that make a later accuracy improvement prove it did not come from leakage or from refitting to one case. Concerns fitted predictions, not rubric points awarded by a judge. Use when a validation number looks too good, when adding a feature to a model already calibrated, or when someone asks whether a model could be cheating. Trigger phrases include target leakage, data leakage, train-test contamination, too good to be true accuracy, feature audit, holdout, is the model cheating, backtest, overfitting to one case, calibration drift.

skills.name: defensible-submission-scoring
skills.description: Score human submissions to a themed call so the result survives a losing team asking why. Reads the problem statement before the submission, runs disqualifying checks before any scoring, scores desirability and survivability on two separate rubrics it carries, and refuses to collapse them into one ranking number because the useful finding lives in the gap between them. For human entries, not model output. Use when judging a hackathon, an innovation competition, a grant round, an internal proposal review, or when aggregating multiple judges' scores into a defensible total. Trigger phrases include judge the submissions, score the demos, apply the rubric, weighted totals, pick the winner, rank the proposals, why did we lose, tie-break, judging tracker.

skills.name: INNOVATION_LIFECYCLE
skills.description: The canonical lifecycle that every hackathon submission must be forced through. Each stage is scored as `COMPLETE`, `PARTIAL`, `MISSING`, or `INVALIDATED`. No stage can be skipped — skipping is the thing hackathons are best at, and this skill exists to catch it.

skills.name: llm-behavior-benchmark
skills.description: Execute an existing rubric across several models or prompts so the resulting ranking survives being contested. Pins the run to a content-hashed manifest, gives every candidate byte-identical inputs, judges with a pinned judge model at fixed temperature, computes the composite once, keeps errors distinguishable from bad scores, and proves the judge discriminates before anything is published. Consumes a rubric; designing one is `anchored-rubric-design`. Use when comparing models on a behavior rather than an answer key, standing up a recurring eval, or investigating why every candidate scores the same. Trigger phrases include benchmark these models, compare models, model bake-off, LLM as judge, eval harness, leaderboard, our eval shows no difference, weekly eval, which model should we use.

skills.name: operational-message-friction
skills.description: Score one unsent operational message against a five-component friction rubric, then compress it only if the score earns a rewrite. Covers the four structural moves every working message needs, per-component bands, channel length targets, and the relationship and audience flags that scoring alone misses. Scores a draft for its reader's cost, not model output or submissions. Use before posting a Slack update, sending an announcement, writing a handoff, or asking for a decision by email. Trigger phrases include score this, friction check, how bad is this, where is the friction, is this too long for Slack, tighten this message, make this Slack-ready, compress this before I send it. Not for essays, posts, or anything where density is the point.

skills.name: ralph-loop
skills.description: A two-pass quality gate that catches the optimism bias inherent in first-pass reviews. Pass 1 checks completeness against source-of-truth artifacts. Pass 2 looks backward and asks "what did we falsely assume?"

skills.name: architecture-note-routing
skills.description: Take raw architectural thinking — a transcript fragment, voice note, research memo, or half-formed idea in chat — and land it in exactly one durable place without inventing detail, duplicating what already exists, or quietly reconciling a contradiction. Classifies the fragment first, then routes it — a term to the glossary, a boundary to an architecture document, a framing to a product document, a closed-off option to a decision record, an unanswered question to the open-questions list. Exists because the default outcome is a new file that overlaps three existing ones. Use when someone drops in raw thinking that needs a home. Trigger phrases include write this up, capture this, where should this live, turn this into a doc, document this idea, synthesise these notes, from this transcript.

skills.name: architecture-note-synthesis
skills.description: Turn a rough architecture fragment, transcript excerpt, or voice-note idea about Jungl3 into the right file(s) under docs/ — routed per CLAUDE.md §7, linked to the glossary, and without inventing detail. Use when the user drops in raw architectural thinking (a paragraph, a transcript, a research memo excerpt, a whiteboard-style idea) and it needs to land somewhere durable rather than stay in chat.

skills.name: corpus_navigation_sync
skills.description: Keep the research corpus **traversable by AI agents** whenever reports are added, removed, renamed, or grouped under a new section.

skills.name: cross_report_synthesis
skills.description: Synthesize findings from multiple research reports into a coherent answer while preserving source traceability and acknowledging uncertainty.

skills.name: customer-interview-synthesis
skills.description: Gate a set of customer interviews before their themes become proposal-grade conclusions. Requires the team's prior hypothesis as an input, enforces a minimum transcript count below which output is forced to exploratory, strips any bias flag that cannot quote the panel or a transcript, and refuses to let an interviewer's notes ground a claim about what a respondent actually did. Use when the risk is that the team's prior comes back dressed as customer signal. Not an interview guide generator and not a theme extractor — it is the check on one. Trigger phrases include is this research actually validated, did the interviews confirm what we already believed, bias check on our research, can we build a proposal on this panel, how many interviews is enough, synthesize our user research.

skills.name: dataset_mapper
skills.description: Identify usable datasets, schemas, access paths, and gaps.

skills.name: evidence_grounded_answering
skills.description: Answer user questions using only content actually present in this repository corpus, with explicit grounding and uncertainty marking.

skills.name: evidence-grounded-verification
skills.description: Clear every load-bearing claim in a document before it reaches someone who can check it. Sorts each claim into do-not-cite, correct-before-use, or cleared; records where you looked; separates measured numbers from derived ones, and unverified from false. Catches claims that feel established only because your own team has repeated them. Use before sending a grant application, board memo, regulatory filing, investor update, press release, conference talk, or README, or when someone asks "are we sure about this?" Trigger phrases include fact check, verify claims, source this, check our numbers, provenance, before we send this, is this actually true.

skills.name: graph_entity_naming
skills.description: Rules for what a knowledge-graph node may be named after, and an audit script that finds junk labels. Use when writing or reviewing extraction parsers, when a graph shows nonsense node titles, when deciding what becomes an entity versus evidence, or before publishing regenerated graph data.

skills.name: jtbd-research
skills.description: After JTBD analysis produces open questions for a pillar, this skill groups them into efficient Parallel AI research queries, fires them, polls for results, and integrates answers back into the JTBD files.

skills.name: knowledge_graph_pipeline
skills.description: Change the knowledge-graph extractor and publish the result across all seven pillar repos and the rvahacks site. Use when editing anything under knowledge-graph/extraction/, when graph data needs regenerating, when running the release check, or when asked to publish or deploy graph changes to rvahacks.org.

skills.name: markdown-knowledge-graph-traversal
skills.description: Answer a hard question from a corpus of plain Markdown notes without producing confident soup. Two-pass hybrid retrieval, a typed claim-and-evidence graph, confidence and source quality scored as separate axes, and a seven-section answer with exact file-path citations. Says "not in the corpus" instead of filling gaps from general knowledge. Answers questions from a corpus; does not repair note-level metadata (markdown-memory-schema-maintenance) or corpus-level indexes (research-corpus-self-indexing). Use for cross-topic, evaluative, decision, provenance, or contradiction-hunting questions over notes, a wiki, a vault, a docs tree, or a research archive. Trigger phrases include ask my notes, what does my vault say, based on my notes, how do we know that, is anything in my notes inconsistent, what have I decided about, which option does the evidence support, search my knowledge base.

skills.name: markdown-memory-schema-maintenance
skills.description: Audit and repair the metadata layer of a Markdown notes corpus, one note at a time, so retrieval and confidence calibration can work. Checks required frontmatter fields, enum validity, stale claim caches, supersede chains, broken wikilinks, orphans, and missing uncertainty labels; emits a defect list ranked by retrieval impact plus an append-only repair plan. Never deletes, never backfills a field value it cannot source. Works inside notes; not the corpus-level index or filing scheme (research-corpus-self-indexing), and never answers a question about the notes' subject matter (markdown-knowledge-graph-traversal). Use after a bulk import, before trusting a corpus for grounded answering, or when search keeps missing notes you know exist. Trigger phrases include audit my vault, validate frontmatter, why can't it find that note, my notes are a mess, check my knowledge base for inconsistencies, find orphan notes, fix my metadata, is my schema still valid.

skills.name: prior-art-regional-research
skills.description: Research what has already been built — regionally and nationally — before generating solution ideas. Ensures ideas are grounded in what is known to work, what has been tried and failed, and what Richmond could adopt or adapt rather than rebuild from scratch.

skills.name: repo_librarian
skills.description: Help users navigate repository knowledge quickly.

skills.name: repo_memory
skills.description: Reconstruct repository state and current stage.

skills.name: report_update_protocol
skills.description: Safely add or update research reports and keep all metadata, indexes, and navigation files synchronized.

skills.name: research_corpus_navigation
skills.description: Map a user question to the correct pillar section and specific research reports before attempting to answer.

skills.name: research-corpus-self-indexing
skills.description: Keep a growing Markdown corpus findable by maintaining the layer above individual notes — verify the generated index still matches its generator, that every dated capture has been promoted into a durable typed note, and that the filing taxonomy is still a closed set. Emits a corpus health report and an ordered repair plan. Never deletes a note, never hand-edits a generated index, never invents a taxonomy the corpus does not declare. Works above the note; not per-note frontmatter validity (markdown-memory-schema-maintenance), and never answers a question from the notes (markdown-knowledge-graph-traversal). Use when a note pile has outgrown the folder it started in, after an ingest pipeline has run unattended for weeks, when two indexes disagree, or before restructuring paths that other tools write to. Trigger phrases include is my index stale, rebuild the index, did the ingest miss anything, my notes never got filed, these captures were never promoted, my vault outgrew its structure, reorganize my knowledge base, which index is right, safe to move these folders.

skills.name: research_runner
skills.description: Execute research prompts and collect findings with sources.

skills.name: research_search
skills.description: Use when answering questions that require facts, evidence, personas, data sources, risks, or prior art from the Thriving Economy pillar research corpus. Use when a team asks about Richmond MBE contracting, small business formation, services, data availability, MVP feasibility, demo strategy, or risks — before answering from memory.

skills.name: run_knowledge_graph
skills.description: Install and run the Knowledge Graph and 3D Funding Explorer visualization

skills.name: amazon-writing-linter
skills.description: Rewrite docs into clear, evidence-heavy Amazon-style prose. Strips vague adjectives, unsupported claims, passive evasions, and weasel words; demands metrics, owners, and decision relevance. Use when polishing a PRFAQ, six-page narrative, memo, or any decision-bearing document; when the user asks to "tighten", "edit", or "make this Amazon-style"; or when a draft is full of "we believe", "significant", "robust", or "simple".

skills.name: annotation-interpretation
skills.description: Interpret scanned or photographed pages of the printed Hardcopy Draft artifacts — locate marks with S{n}P{m} anchors and Q{n} question ids, classify symbols/dials/directives per MARKUP.md, decide what is an edit vs. a note vs. noise, and report ambiguity instead of guessing. Use for tasks about reading marked-up pages, handwriting recognition prompts, resolving annotations to blocks, or applying pen edits to a document.

skills.name: communication-rollout-planning
skills.description: Sequence a multi-channel announcement into an ordered plan of communication moves with draft copy for each, ordered so nobody who matters hears it from a broadcast. Covers audience size bands, composition, how each segment stands toward the sender, which move fits which purpose, and the ordering rules that decide what has to happen before the broadcast. Use when planning a launch, reorg, policy change, decision, migration, or any announcement with stakeholders. Trigger phrases include comm plan, how should I roll this out, plan the announcement, who do I need to tell first, sequence this rollout, launch plan, change management. Not for drafting or scoring one message.

skills.name: decision-prose-linting
skills.description: Tighten a decision-bearing draft — memo, brief, proposal, status narrative — without making it more confident than the author was. A removed hedge must be replaced by an explicit uncertainty tag rather than left as a bald assertion, and every removal is logged in a ledger so the author can confirm nothing load-bearing was lost. Never invents a number, an owner, or a date to satisfy its own rules. Use when a draft is going to a reviewer who will ask how you know. Trigger phrases include tighten this, lint this doc, remove the fluff, make this evidence-based, edit this memo, this reads like marketing, cut the weasel words, before I send this to leadership.

skills.name: paper-markup-revision
skills.description: Apply edits marked by hand on a printed draft back into the source file, resolving every positional reference to an exact block or refusing to guess. Covers printing with deterministic S{n}P{m} margin anchors, the mark vocabulary, the resolution order, and an unresolved file no instruction can be dropped from silently. Use after marking up a printout, dictating changes against a paper copy, or transcribing red-pen edits. Trigger phrases include apply my edits, I marked up the printout, merge my dictated changes, here are my markup notes, v2 with my edits, apply the red pen. Not for rewriting a draft in a voice and not for proofreading.

skills.name: research-grounded-outreach
skills.description: Draft SME outreach emails that lead with confirmed research findings and ask only the questions that genuinely remain unanswered. Replaces the generic `sme-outreach` skill template with a research-heavy format that earns credibility before making asks.

skills.name: six-page-narrative
skills.description: Convert a strategy, architecture, or major decision into a six-page narrative — a written decision memo with context, problem, current state, proposed mechanism, alternatives, risks, metrics, and explicit dissent. No slides. No bullet soup. Use when preparing a decision document for senior review, when an architecture needs written defense, or when the user mentions "six-pager", "narrative", "decision memo", "strategy doc", or "ADR but bigger".

skills.name: sme-outreach
skills.description: Draft a ready-to-send email to a subject matter expert (city staff, nonprofit professional, or community organization) asking specific questions that only a human with lived experience or institutional access can answer.

skills.name: synthesize
skills.description: The single transformation primitive of Hardcopy Tools' synthesize contract (vendored from markdown-soul). Takes Markdown content + a required brief.md (persona, voice, throughline, channels, stakes) + a constraint bundle and returns brief-faithful Markdown. REFUSES to run without a brief — voice resolves from ~/.me/voices/<name>.md, channels from ~/.me/channels/<name>.md. Outputs land in .output/<bundle>/<channel>/{post,to-research,tighten,unresolved,synthesis-map}.md. Bundles live in bundles/<name>/BUNDLE.md and declare non-voice references plus a mode (edit, synthesis, polish, compress). Use when the user asks to apply hand-marked edits to a draft, weave a new post from source materials, refactor or tighten a draft in their voice, elevate raw notes into a publishable piece, compress an operational message to KSP structure, rewrite for Slack, or any other "Markdown in → brief-faithful Markdown out" transformation. Trigger phrases include "apply my edits", "compose from these sources", "weave these into a post", "refactor this draft", "tighten this", "rewrite in my voice", "elevate this", "compress this", "KSP this". Auto-detects the appropriate bundle from input shape and dictation; user can name the bundle explicitly. Not for scoring (see ksp-score) or multi-channel rollout sequencing (see comm-plan).

skills.name: voice-faithful-drafting
skills.description: Draft, rewrite, or weave a long-form piece in one named person's voice, governed by a required brief stating persona, throughline, channel, and stakes. Refuses to run without the brief, and refuses to infer persona or throughline from the source material. Use when rewriting a draft in someone's voice, elevating notes or a transcript into a publishable piece, weaving several sources into one post, or producing one piece for several channels. Trigger phrases include rewrite this in my voice, tighten this draft, refactor this post, elevate these notes, polish this, weave these into a post, compose from these sources, make this publishable. Not for operational messages, proofreading, or fact-checking.

skills.name: adr-author
skills.description: Write a new Architecture Decision Record for Jungl3 under docs/decisions/, matching the Nygard-trimmed format established by ADRs 0001–0003. Use when a decision has been made that closes off options, resolves an open question from CLAUDE.md §11, or makes a choice costly to reverse — and the decision is ready to be pinned rather than left ambient in chat.

skills.name: billing-and-credits
skills.description: Change anything money-adjacent — credit packs, the credit ledger, reservations, Stripe checkout, the Stripe webhook, purchase records, refunds/chargebacks, the paywall, or the billing page. Use for tasks mentioning credits, balance, checkout, Stripe, prices, purchases, paywall, refunds, or "Get credits". The detailed money rules live in docs/BILLING.md; this skill routes you to them and to the code that implements them.

skills.name: compliance-control-audit
skills.description: Audit running cloud infrastructure against a named control set and produce findings an auditor can re-derive and an engineer can act on. Reports what was not checked as loudly as what failed. Read-only; never changes infrastructure. Use before an audit window, after an infrastructure change, or when someone asks how compliant an account is. Trigger phrases include compliance audit, SOC 2 evidence, control gap analysis, are we compliant, findings report, security posture review, check our controls, audit readiness, CIS benchmark check.

skills.name: corpus-transform
skills.description: Design an expensive, long-running transformation over a large corpus so that a crash loses at most one item, a resume neither duplicates nor skips work, partial output is never mistaken for a complete corpus, and spend stops at a ceiling you chose. Covers checkpoint key design, atomic writes, validate-before-write ordering, and per-item versus run-level failure handling. Use when running a paid model or API over thousands of records, enriching a whole dataset, backfilling a table, or re-running a job that died partway. Trigger phrases include batch process, run over the whole corpus, resume from checkpoint, it died halfway, backfill, bulk enrich, how much will this cost, pick up where it left off, idempotent pipeline.
